description: CONCORD. We are a team working on the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. We are building a custom data analysis tool that integrates Python with an interactive dashboard and physical hardware to analyze and visualize significant Earth science data anomalies.
summary: CONCORDE (Coupled Observatory Node for Climate Outliers and Regime Detection at the Edge) is an Edge-to-Core climate intelligence platform built to help researchers, students, and policymakers separate true long-term climate signals from seasonal weather noise. Raw monthly satellite records swing sharply between seasons, masking gradual multi-decade shifts and multi-variable feedbacks. CONCORDE pairs a physical ESP32 hardware node (Dual-IR occupancy sensors, PN532 NFC biome scanner, 0.96" OLED, and a 5-LED alert matrix) with a Python/Streamlit cloud observatory connected to 36 years (1990–2025) of NASA POWER, MERRA-2, and CERES satellite archives. Using guided biome questionnaires or Gemini 2.5 Flash natural-language routing, CONCORDE deseasonalizes 4-variable clusters, tests statistical significance, detects CUSUM regime tipping points, forecasts 10-year trajectories, and broadcasts real-time hardware alerts.

────────────────────────────────────────

1. WHAT DOES CONCORDE DO?

CONCORDE (Coupled Observatory Node for Climate Outliers and Regime Detection at the Edge) is a dual hardware-and-cloud Earth observation detective system. It solves three fundamental challenges in environmental data analysis:

1) The Seasonal Zig-Zag Trap: Raw monthly satellite measurements oscillate wildly between summer and winter, hiding gradual multi-decade shifts until the 1990–2025 monthly climatological baseline is removed.

2) Observation Window Blindness: Analyzing short 10-to-13-year windows frequently yields statistically unconfirmed results (p ≥ 0.05) due to interannual weather noise, whereas 36-year records reveal structural shifts.

3) Single-Variable Isolation: Examining temperature or precipitation alone misses coupled physical feedbacks across thermal (T2M), radiative (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), hydrological (PRECTOTCORR, GWETTOP, QV2M), and aerodynamic (WS2M) parameters.

────────────────────────────────────────

2. HOW DOES IT WORK? (END-TO-END ARCHITECTURE)

A. Physical Edge Node (ESP32 / C++)

• Dual-IR Gate & Occupancy Detection: Senses when a researcher enters the laboratory and wakes the telemetry node.

• PN532 NFC Biome Scanner: Scanning physical regional NFC cards (e.g., Berrechid, Casablanca, Ouarzazate, Sebou, Amazon, Svalbard) synchronizes the cloud dashboard to the active regional investigation via HTTP /status polling.

• Real-Time UDP Telemetry (Port 4210) & 5-LED Alert Matrix: Once the cloud engine completes its mathematical pipeline, it transmits a compact UDP packet (TARGET|SLOPE_DEC|STRONGEST_DRIVER|CORR|TIP_YEAR|PRED_END|BITMASK_5LEDS) back to the ESP32 to display status on a 0.96" OLED screen and trigger 5 tactical alert LEDs:

- LED 1 (Blue): Significant Hydrological Trend (p < 0.05 on PRECTOTCORR, GWETTOP, or QV2M)

- LED 2 (Orange): CUSUM Regime Acceleration (≥ 1.4× post-inflection slope shift)

- LED 3 (Red): High-Confidence Climate Anomaly (Mann-Kendall p < 0.01)

- LED 4 (White): Inverse Driver-Target Paradox Coupling (opposite slopes with |r| ≥ 0.35)

- LED 5 (Green): System Within Natural Baseline Variability

B. Dual Inquiry Modes & Data Ingestion

• Guided 3-Step Detective Questionnaire: Users select a Biome Archetype, a Research Question, and a Record Length (36, 21, or 13 annual means), automatically pairing 1 Target Variable with 3 physically coupled Driver Variables.

• AI Natural-Language Query Router: Powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash (with a deterministic local domain fallback and Open-Meteo geocoding), translating plain-English prompts into a 4-variable NASA POWER API request.

• External CSV Ingestion: Supports custom monthly time-series uploads from NASA Giovanni, AppEEARS, NOAA CDO, and CUAHSI.

C. The 4-Layer Scientific Intelligence Engine (Python / Pandas / SciPy / Scikit-Learn)

• Layer 1 — Deseasonalized Trend & Sufficiency Analysis: Computes monthly climatology subtraction, OLS linear decadal slopes (±95% confidence interval fan), non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend tests (S, Z, p), Sen's median slope, Student's t-test, Isolation Forest extreme-year detection, and an Observation Window Sufficiency Estimator calculating how many additional years of observation are required to reach p < 0.05.

• Layer 2 — Cross-Correlation, Lag & Paradox Matrix: Evaluates a 4×4 deseasonalized correlation heatmap, tests 0-to-3 month lagged responses, and flags Inverse Paradoxes.

• Layer 3 — Piecewise CUSUM Tipping-Point Detection: Identifies the structural inflection year and computes pre- vs. post-split decadal slope acceleration.

• Layer 4 — Hybrid AI Forecast & "What If?" Simulator: Generates a 10-year multivariate projection using a Random Forest Regressor and an Intel OpenVINO IR Graph (with NumPy fallback), paired with interactive ±3σ driver perturbation sliders.

D. Cross-Regional Watchlist & Z-Score Comparison

• Archives investigated regions as interactive session chips and overlays any two biomes on a dimensionless Z-score (σ) scale to detect divergent climate regimes.

────────────────────────────────────────

3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED

• Hardware & Embedded: ESP32 Microcontroller, C++ (PlatformIO / VS Code), PN532 NFC Reader, Dual-IR Obstacle Sensors, 0.96" I2C OLED Display, 5-Channel LED Matrix, Wi-Fi UDP/HTTP Telemetry, Firebase Realtime Database sync.

• Cloud & Data Science Stack: Python 3.12, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Scikit-Learn, Intel OpenVINO Runtime, Plotly, Requests.

• AI & Transparency Disclosure: Gemini 2.5 Flash API is optionally used for natural-language prompt routing into NASA variable codes; Scikit-Learn (Random Forest / Isolation Forest) and Intel OpenVINO are used for statistical forecasting; AI coding and design assistants were used for code review, documentation formatting, and brand asset generation. All scientific computations run deterministically on authentic NASA satellite observations.
